headline: Permits and Logistics for West Virginia’s Deepest Gorge
reservation: New River Gorge National Park and Preserve does not currently require a general entry permit, but specific activities like commercial whitewater rafting and group camping must be booked through official outfitters or the federal reservation system. Check the official NPS site for seasonal facility closures and changes to the Bridge Day access rules.

days.title: Rim Views and Historic Spans

stops.name: Canyon Rim Visitor Center
stops.detail: View the New River Gorge Bridge from the boardwalks and gather orientation maps from park staff.

stops.name: Endless Wall Trail
stops.detail: Hike the cliff-top path for expansive views of the river and the sandstone strata popular with climbers.

days.driving: Allow 20–30 minutes between local trailheads; conditions vary.
days.note: Stay on marked boardwalks at overlooks to protect the fragile cliff-edge ecosystem.

days.title: Gorge Depth and Industrial Heritage

stops.name: Fayette Station Road
stops.detail: Drive this winding historic route to reach the river level and view the bridge from below.

stops.name: Thurmond Historic District
stops.detail: Explore the preserved railroad town that served as a major coal hub in the early 20th century.

days.driving: Allow 60–90 minutes for the winding drive to Thurmond; conditions vary.
days.note: Fayette Station Road is narrow with hairpins; check vehicle length restrictions before descending.

days.title: Southern Falls and River Vistas

stops.name: Sandstone Falls
stops.detail: Walk the boardwalk to see the river spanning 1,500 feet across a series of dramatic drops.

stops.name: Grandview Overlook
stops.detail: Visit the Main Overlook for a classic view of the New River’s horseshoe bend from 1,400 feet above.

days.driving: Allow 1.5–2 hours to transit between the northern and southern park units; conditions vary.
days.note: The southern portion of the park is remote; ensure you have a full tank of fuel.

intel.title: Trailhead Capacity
intel.text: Parking lots at Long Point and Endless Wall are small and often reach capacity during autumn weekends. Have a secondary trail in mind if primary lots are full to avoid parking on narrow road shoulders.

intel.title: Gorge Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular reception is extremely limited at the bottom of the gorge and in remote areas like Thurmond. Download offline maps and park brochures at the visitor center before departing.

intel.title: Gateway Fuel Stations
intel.text: Major fueling stations are concentrated in Fayetteville and Beckley. There are very limited services within the park boundaries or along the river access roads.

intel.title: Bridge Day Constraints
intel.text: The third Saturday in October involves significant road closures and massive crowds for the annual Bridge Day event. Check official local traffic advisories if visiting during the peak foliage season.

intel.title: Winter Road Conditions
intel.text: Steep access roads into the gorge may become impassable or close during snow and ice events. Check the official NPS 'Alerts' page for daily updates on road status during the winter months.

plan.arrival: Arrive at BKW and drive 53 minutes to Fayetteville to stock up on supplies and check in to your base near the northern gorge access.
plan.vehicle: A vehicle with high clearance is beneficial for some gravel access roads; check rental restrictions for off-pavement use.
plan.goldenHour: Long Point Overlook provides a direct view of the bridge, though cloud cover in the gorge often dictates visibility.
